summary:
Sort the weights. For each choice of the smallest weight `a[i]`, the other two must add up to `target − a[i]`
among the weights after it, which two pointers from both ends find in linear time. O(n²) overall, O(1) extra
space.

question.md:
Decide whether three weights at different positions add up to exactly `target`.

- **Different positions**, but equal weights are allowed (two 5-gram weights can both be used).
- **Up to 500 weights**: O(n³) is about 2 × 10⁷ triples, O(n²) is 2.5 × 10⁵ steps.

think.md:
Weights `[12, 3, 7, 1, 9, 20]`, target 28: 1 + 7 + 20 = 28, so **true**.

Three unknowns are hard; two are easy. Fix the first weight, and the problem becomes "find two weights with sum
`target − first`", which in a sorted list is the two-pointer squeeze. To avoid counting the same weight twice,
only search to the right of the fixed one.

idea.md: Three nested loops over `i < j < k`.

steps.text: Weights [12, 7, 9] at positions [0, 2, 4] add up to 28.

walk.title: Try every triple of different positions.

limits.md: The innermost loop just searches for one value, `target − w[i] − w[j]`. Sorting lets two pointers find the last two weights together in linear time.

idea.md: Sort. For each `i`, set `j = i + 1`, `k = n − 1` and squeeze: sum too small → `j++`, too big → `k−−`, equal → true.

lines.text: The smallest weight of the triple is `a[i]`; the other two come from positions after `i`.
Two-pointer search for the remaining pair: too small → raise the low end, too big → lower the high end.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²)** (plus the sort). **Space O(n)** for the sorted copy, O(1) besides.

steps.text: Fix 1: 1 + 3 + 20 = 24, too small: move j right.

walk.title: Sort. Fix the smallest weight of the triple, then find the other two with pointers from both ends of the rest.

takeaways.md:
- **3-sum = fix one + 2-sum.** Sorting makes the inner 2-sum a linear squeeze.
- Only search to the right of the fixed element so each triple is considered once.
- 4-sum: fix two, squeeze two (O(n³)).
